headword: {被修飾語|ひしゅうしょくご}
gloss: modified word; head word (the word that a modifier modifies)

definitions.gloss: modified word; head word (the word that a modifier modifies)
definitions.explanation: A linguistic term referring to the word that receives modification from another word (the modifier). In the phrase "red apple," "apple" is the modified word and "red" is the modifier. Used in grammar textbooks, linguistics papers, and Japanese-language teaching.

examples.japanese: ⟦{修飾語|しゅうしょくご}→修飾語：21309_shuushokugo⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{被修飾語|ひしゅうしょくご}。
examples.english: The modifier and the modified word.

examples.japanese: {被修飾語|ひしゅうしょくご}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{通常|つうじょう}→通常：27316_tsuujou⟧、⟦{修飾語|しゅうしょくご}→修飾語：21309_shuushokugo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{後|あと}→後：09580_ato⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{来|く}る→来る：00254_kuru⟧。
examples.english: In Japanese, the modified word usually comes after the modifier.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{文|ぶん}→文：03716_bun⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧「{本|ほん}」⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{被修飾語|ひしゅうしょくご}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧、「⟦{赤|あか}い→赤い：00585_akai⟧」⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{修飾語|しゅうしょくご}→修飾語：21309_shuushokugo⟧⟦である→である：09855_dearu⟧。
examples.english: In this sentence, "book" is the modified word and "red" is the modifier.

examples.japanese: ⟦{日本語|にほんご}→日本語：00614_nihongo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{文法|ぶんぽう}→文法：01506_bunpou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{修飾語|しゅうしょくご}→修飾語：21309_shuushokugo⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{被修飾語|ひしゅうしょくご}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{関係|かんけい}→関係：01298_kankei⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{正|ただ}しく→正しい：00893_tadashii⟧⟦{把握|はあく}する→把握する：19628_haakusuru⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{重要|じゅうよう}→重要：01575_juuyou⟧だ。
examples.english: In Japanese grammar, it is important to grasp correctly the relationship between the modifier and the modified word.

notes:
Composed of the passive prefix {被|ひ} (receiving; undergoing), ⟦{修飾|しゅうしょく}→修飾：00460_shuushoku⟧ (modification; qualification), and ⟦{語|ご}→〜語：09841_go⟧ (word). Literally "the word that receives modification" — the prefix {被|ひ} marks the receiving side, just as in ⟦{被害者|ひがいしゃ}→被害者：14106_higaisha⟧ (victim) and ⟦{被告|ひこく}→被告：11080_hikoku⟧ (defendant).

USAGE:
A grammar term. You will see it in Japanese-language textbooks, school grammar lessons, linguistic papers, and Japanese-as-a-foreign-language teaching materials. It is almost always paired with ⟦{修飾語|しゅうしょくご}→修飾語：21309_shuushokugo⟧ (modifier). In Japanese, the {被修飾語|ひしゅうしょくご} comes AFTER the modifier, which is the opposite of the order in many European languages but the same as English attributive order.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{修飾語|しゅうしょくご}→修飾語：21309_shuushokugo⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{被修飾語|ひしゅうしょくご}: modifier and modified word
- {被修飾語|ひしゅうしょくご}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{修飾|しゅうしょく}→修飾：00460_shuushoku⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to modify the head word
- {被修飾語|ひしゅうしょくご}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{関係|かんけい}→関係：01298_kankei⟧: the modifier-head relationship

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{修飾語|しゅうしょくご}→修飾語：21309_shuushokugo⟧: modifier — the counterpart; the word doing the modifying
- ⟦{主語|しゅご}→主語：00377_shugo⟧: subject — a different grammatical role; not about modification
- {連体修飾語|れんたいしゅうしょくご}: nominal modifier — a more specific term for a modifier that attaches to a noun
- {係|かか}る・⟦{受|う}ける→受ける：01215_ukeru⟧: to modify / to be modified (as verbs) — describes the same relationship in action
